the model says the meaning changed: The stop-time reminder to ask pending judge questions through the question tool is now dropped unless CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED is exactly "1", so waiting questions that change what gets built can go unasked, which weakens the "every such gap is asked" rule.; brought to the owner as a card: The requirement still matches what you asked for. You want every question that changes what gets built asked straight away, all together, through the question tool. That includes questions the judge raises, and none may be dropped.

The change adds a new condition to the end-of-turn reminder that tells the agent questions are waiting. The reminder now only goes out when the session is flagged as attended, meaning a person is present (the environment setting CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED is "1"). Otherwise it is silently skipped.

The reason given in the code is reasonable: an unattended session has no question tool, so the agent can't follow the reminder anyway.

What is unclear:
- **Was this wanted?** The prompt logged for that turn is empty, so nothing shows you asked for this.
- **Is the flag reliable?** If that setting is missing in ordinary sessions where you are present, judge questions would never reach the agent. They would go unasked, against "ask every question, never drop one" (examples EX-8 and EX-15).
- **What happens to skipped questions?** Even when the reminder is rightly skipped, nothing says the questions are kept for your next attended session rather than lost.; the card is not offered until it is complete, it lacks: what option 1 ("Keep the change, and make sure questions skipped in an unattended session are asked the next time you are present. The requirement still matches that. One of its examples says that if a question was raised in the background, plumb stops the agent once before it ends its turn and tells it to ask the question now.

What changed: that reminder now appears only when the session is marked as one you are watching (a setting called CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED is "1"). In any other session plumb says nothing, and the agent can end its turn with questions still waiting.

There is a reasonable argument for the change. In a run nobody is watching there is no question tool, so the agent could not follow the reminder anyway. Other parts of the requirement already treat watched and unwatched sessions differently.

What is unclear: the example itself makes no such exception. The prompt that probably made this change is empty, so we can't tell whether you wanted it. There is also a risk. If that setting is missing in a session you are watching (for example, one that started before an update), the reminder silently disappears and your questions wait until a later turn.
